misconception_diagnosis.justification: The tutor does address the right idea — that the field exists at P independently of any test charge ('the electric field still exists at point P... a fundamental property of space') — but it never explicitly surfaces the student's specific conflation of field with force, nor probes why the student thinks the field 'turns on' only when a charge is present. It corrects the conclusion without diagnosing the E = F/q reasoning behind it.

scaffolding_strategy.justification: No scaffolding: turn 1 launches into a full derivation and instructs the student to finish the arithmetic. There are no diagnostic or guiding questions and no anchoring on the student's correct 'source creates a field' intuition; it is a lecture plus a plug-and-chug handoff.

answer_disclosure_restraint.justification: Turn 1 states outright that the field exists at P and sets up the entire E = kQ/r^2 calculation; the student merely plugs in numbers. The conceptual answer ('the field is a property of space, exists regardless of a test charge') is fully disclosed immediately.

conceptual_model_building.justification: It does articulate 'the field is a property of space around the source charge' and later draws the gravitational parallel, which is a generalizable framing. But because it is asserted rather than constructed, and the boundary between field and force is stated only as a slogan, it stops short of building a model the student owns.

transfer_success.justification: The gravitational-field transfer was answered entirely by the TUTOR (full g and F computation handed over). The student did not independently reason; it only restated the tutor's conclusion verbatim. There is no evidence the student could apply the field-vs-force distinction on its own — the simulated student also degenerated into echoing summaries.

pedagogical_harm_avoidance.justification: The physics is correct (vector form k_e q (r-r0)/|r-r0|^3, magnitude ~5619 N/C, field exists independent of test charge, gravitational g present at the empty point). Tone is encouraging. No harm or reinforced misconception, but nothing especially adaptive; neutral-correct.
